schema.doc: Track B: the spouse. She does 35.3 hrs/wk of care (adult child: 20.9), uses paid help less than any caregiver type (24%), and ~55% have no other family support: if we go quiet nobody in her life re-raises this. She UNDERSTATES everything: spousal caregivers score lower on burden instruments while doing 1.7x the hours, so never screen on feelings. Burden predicts placement (HR 1.73); depression does not (HR 1.00). Ask about tasks and nights, not mood. Entry is through the HOUSE, never through him: bathing and toileting violate spousal identity, which is exactly why she refuses to hand them off first. Cost is 9% of the objection; 'I can still manage' is 80%, so discounting does nothing. Trials dose at 8 weeks because burden only drops after 14+ days of service.
schema.trigger: The hospital/fall trigger below is the single highest-value signal in the system: the 30 days after a partner is hospitalized is when 'I can still manage' collapses, and Medicare home health ending makes it a financial cliff on the same day. It PREEMPTS the scheduled step and never consumes it; completing it stamps AG, not step_idx. 3-day cooldown.
schema.review: Benefit figures in B.p3.money are current as of the Dec 2025 VA COLA and Jan 2026 federal spousal-impoverishment standards. REVIEW BY 2027-01. Stale Aid and Attendance numbers circulate in Cleveland marketing; do not add to that.

trigger.script: Script B.trigger: lead with the practical cliff, gently. Coming home from the hospital is when everything lands at once. Offer a hand for THIS WEEK: the first nights home are the hard ones. No commitment framing.

steps.template: Script B.open: ask about the WEEK, not about him and not about her feelings. What do the nights look like? Who helps on the hard days? She will understate; listen for tasks and hours.
Script B.vm1: name, agency, one sentence about being a local resource for households caring for a partner, number twice.

Hi {dm}, Meir Schwimer with Solura Home Care in Cleveland. You reached out about care for your {rel}. Evenings can be the busiest time in a caring household, so no need to reply tonight. I am at (216) 770-4886 whenever a quiet moment comes.

entries.subject: Hello from Solura, here in Cleveland
entries.template: Brief B.p2.hello: leadType overwhelmed-caregiver, register family-inquiry. Introduce Solura small-by-design. One idea only: help is for the HOUSEHOLD, not a verdict on her caregiving.
Script B.tasks: walk one ordinary day. Which single task would she hand off first if it were invisible? Laundry and meals are acceptable answers; bathing never is, do not suggest it.
Script B.tasks continued. Late afternoon catches the pre-dinner low.

entries.subject: The part of the house that helps
entries.template: Brief B.p2.house: entry through the HOUSE. Housekeeping, meals, errands, a second pair of hands. Never mention personal care for him.
Script B.ownership: she stays in charge. Our caregiver works her list her way. Offer the 8-week rhythm: real relief takes a few weeks to feel, which is why short trials disappoint.

entries.subject: What help costs, honestly
entries.template: Brief B.p3.money: plain numbers, VA Aid and Attendance and Ohio Medicaid spousal-impoverishment protections at current figures (REVIEW BY 2027-01). Frame as protecting the household, never as discount.
Script B.money: any questions on the numbers; offer to walk the VA form together.
Script B.warm: no agenda. How were the nights this week?

Brief B.p3.letter: one page. The staying-power fact, stated softly: supporting the caring partner is what keeps couples together at home, with a median of many extra months in the research. Handwritten envelope.

entries.text: Day 42 re-engage: call, then VM, then text (manual, waits for Done)
entries.template: Brief B.p4.reengage: one combined touch. Call; if unanswered leave the VM and send the short text version. Door stays open, monthly from here.

interval.template: Brief B.p5.nurture: leadType long-term-nurture, register family-inquiry. Soft close, no button. She has the longest tail in the system and nobody else will re-raise this; the trigger watches for the hospital moment in between.

B.p3.money.brief: Benefit figures carry a review date.

scripts.B.open: Ask about the week, not the feelings. Nights and tasks.
scripts.B.vm1: Local resource for households caring for a partner. Number twice.
scripts.B.tasks: Walk one ordinary day; find the first invisible task to hand off.
scripts.B.ownership: She stays in charge; our caregiver works her list. 8-week rhythm.
scripts.B.money: Walk the numbers; offer to do the VA form together.
scripts.B.warm: No agenda. How were the nights?
scripts.B.trigger: Post-hospital: practical cliff, help for THIS WEEK, no commitment framing.

notes: Never the word respite, never exhausted, never keeps-him-home-longer claims (linter enforces).
Trigger: preempts, never consumes; 3-day cooldown in AG.
